newsitem.title: KENYA: Improved demand lifts Nairobi bourse index.
newsitem.headline: Improved demand lifts Nairobi bourse index.

text.p: Improved demand on key shares at the Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) lifted the 20-share index on Monday, brokers and bourse officials said.
The index gained 8.02 points to stand at 3006.98. Turnover was posted at 9.325 million shillings traded on 272,824 shares from 23.798 million shillings traded on 682,839 shares on Friday.
Dealers said the market picked up, boosted especially by foreign investors.
"The market mood hasn't changed much, but once again, foreign transactions took the spotlight," a senior broker said.
Sasini Tea & Coffee gained 1.50 to close at 58, while Kenya Breweries closed at 49 from 48.50.

Kenya Airways eased further to 8.85 from 8.90. Kenya Airways stock was on a downward trend for the whole of last week. Monday's closing price was the lowest it has ever been since it's primary offer of 11.25.
Brokers said investors were disappointed after the airline posted a 6.9 percent fall in net profits before tax in the first six months of the airline's 1996/97 year (April/March).
"It just goes to confirm what I initially thought about Kenya Airways. If you buy the share, you must be willing to be in it for a long time," one broker said.
Kenya Power & Lighting closed at 132 from 131 but Nation Printers and Publishers was unchanged at 107.
"It's very interesting that these two shares have been on an upward trend when most other shares in the market have been fluctuating or declining," the senior broker said.
"Institutional investors appear to feel secure investing in a monopoly like Kenya Power & Lighting Co because its revenue is guaranteed," another said. "It's more like a treasury bill."
Foreign investors bought 3,998 shares of Kenya Commercial Bank at between 57.50 and 58 from 57.50 and 12,700 shares of National Industrial Credit at between 41-42 from 41.
